text_blocks.snippet: Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world, with a peak elevation of 8,848.86 meters (29,031.7 feet) above sea level.

list.snippet: Location: Situated in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range of the Himalayas, on the border between Nepal and Tibet Autonomous Region, China.

snippet_links.text: Nepal and Tibet Autonomous Region, China

list.snippet: Local Names: Known as Sagarmatha in Nepali ("Peak of Heaven") and Chomolungma in Tibetan ("Goddess Mother of the World").
First Ascent: Successfully summitted on May 29, 1953, by Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay.

Tallest from Base to Peak: Mauna Kea in Hawaii is a volcano measuring over 10,210 meters (33,500 feet) from its base on the ocean floor to its peak, making it taller from base to top than Everest. However, its peak is only 4,207 meters above sea level.
